steps.text: The wind rustles the branches in late autumn, the sound of a cello filling the forest matted by fallen leaves.
Amiya treks along to the cello's melodies. Her fist is loosely clenched, rings shimmering faintly beneath the sunlight filtering through the trees.
A black-haired Sankta is standing in a clearing in the forest, embracing her cello, ever so focused.
The sound of the cello continues to flow, uninterrupted by her arrival. A gentle sound.

spans.text: The sound of the cello continues to
, uninterrupted by her arrival. A gentle sound.

steps.text: Amiya stops, and her palms begin to loosen. Gradually, even the trees around her and the clouds above her begin to melt into the flowing stream, seemingly rippling through the sky, yet also around her feet.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Arturia.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You shouldn't just wander from your room as you please. Besides, today, there's a...
The Sankta woman lifts her gaze slightly. There is still a bit of distance separating the two of them, but Amiya is sure that the woman has seen her.
Amiya does not move, instead, the starlight and the waves reach out to embrace her. Across thousands of blurry scenes, countless figures intersect with her.
She feels as if she has become a book, and the cello's melodies a pair of hands, flipping through the deepest pages of her emotions.
Federico warned everyone to stay away from her music.
But, Amiya is not of the same mind.
She quietly takes a deep breath.
This is something only she can do. To touch the face beneath the veil of mystery, to reach Arturia.
Amiya, what are you looking at?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Huh?
Amiya turns when she hears the voice. At some point, a woman as pure as the moonlight approached, her eyes gentle as always.
Amiya sees herself reflected in the eyes of the woman before her–
Sitting in the corner of the deck with her arms tightly hugging her knees, bangs loosely covering her eyes.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Amiya, you've been sitting on the deck all this time. What are you looking at?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Um, the sun is about to set.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: One of the nice men from Engineering gave me a lolly. Theresa, are you done with work?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes, I am. Are you thinking about your mom and dad?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dad used to carry me up to the roof of the work shed after he came back from his Engineering work.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It got pretty cold after the sun went down, but Dad's shoulders were really thick, so we could stay there for a long time.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I remember the stars coming out one by one, until filled up the night sky...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But now, the Doctor is with me. Dr. Kal'tist is with me too, and so are you.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Every now and then... it makes me... miss Mom and Dad a bit less.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The Doctor said that in this last year of sailing the land, you were the motivating factor.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's very fortunate that the Doctor saved you. I'm also glad that Rhodes Island was able to become your home.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Perhaps, death is not the most profound goodbye. But, it is the most cruel, impossible to turn back.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yet, you have faced it bravely.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You may have to endure more goodbyes in the future. But remember, goodbye is not the end.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You will feel. You will connect. You will live on. You will become the place where everything meets. You... will become the future.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Where do you plan to go next?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm going back.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I... Thank you so much.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But, I can't stay here any longer.
The memory of Theresa becomes blurry.
The Lord of Fiends grants illusions unto others. The Lord of Fiends also passes down memories and Arts, as well as emotions and knowledge.
But, Amiya has never delved deeply into herself.
Like a pair of mirrors. Amiya throws open the transparent door.
...and on the other side of the door is a lawn.
It has just rained, and a pleasant scent wafts through the air. A small church stands silent not too far away––
All the guests have already left, leaving only a young Sankta standing in front of a tombstone.
She stands there in silence, water droplets still clinging to her cheeks. She cannot tell if they are rain or tears.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: So, Arturia, is 'death' the theme of this song?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You're suffering. But, look. It took a long time, and meeting a lot of people, to not be so sad when I think of my parents.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But, you're not just sad. There's also confusion... and anger?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Directed at who? The guests who turned their backs and left? Or, 'death' itself?
Yet, Arturia does not truly see her. The young Sankta stands in the shadows of the past.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Mamma, how much courage did it take for you to take that brave step?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: How could death pluck your life from you so quickly?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Why does death turn human bodies into empty husks? Why is it so easy to make all those complex, profound emotions disappear without a trace?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Why are we but wisps of clouds?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: So free, so beautiful, yet gone whenever the wind blows?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It turns all our effort to make up for past regrets into new regrets.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And you shouldn't have... you didn't need to die.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Cora, you didn't need to die.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: There were so many chances for you to leave before the Empresses' celebration began.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: Arturia, you had so many chances to tell me your feelings, in Marigold Alley, at Ludwigs-Universität, even at the theater in front of the spire.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: Did you not know how to express them? Even though you know that I understand your music.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I tried telling Viviana, hoping that she would discover your existence through the clues left in the Güldenesgesatz.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But, even she...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I don't want to change the decision that you made, nor can I.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: That's right. In fact, you know better than anyone that I passed on with no regrets.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: The one with regrets... is you, isn't it?

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: I'll always remember our first meeting, at Lehrer Emmanuel's funeral, beneath the sunset in front of the imperial spires...

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: I helped tune your cello, and you told me about the people you had met and things you had experienced.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: I couldn't see your face clearly, but I could hear the stirring sounds of your cello.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You shared with me your regrets, as well as the faith those regrets brought you. You were the first person who encouraged me to play the melodies of my heart.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You are one of the few close friends I've had on this long, long journey.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I don't want to...

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: But will my feelings, and all the things I've experienced, truly dissipate like flowing clouds?

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: Arturia, my dear friend, play for me. Let me hear your music one more time.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: I've always believed that this is what they precisely meant.
The cello's melodies flow, and more scenes that she has never seen unfold in front of Arturia. Those images and sounds melt into a river, flowing towards reaches unknowable to man.
Arturia wades through the river.
She does not know when or how she reached the shore, but when she next opens her eyes, she finds herself standing in front of a door.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You've come a long way, haven't you?

steps.name: Arturia?
steps.text: Is this a monastery?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A monastery built on a nomadic plate. Looks a lot like Sanctilaminium Ambrosii, doesn't it?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It has roamed the lands with me for many years. But now, it's been still for two and a half months.

steps.name: Arturia?
steps.text: Is it worn down?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: No, it's because I've been sick.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I've been waiting. Waiting for death to come.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: No need to keep looking. I'm the only one here, and no one else is coming.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: We're a long way from Laterano. So far that even the legati who crossed countless lands for the Lateran Declaration have never tread.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I know what you're here for, Arturia.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The reason an ideal can be an ideal is that it is sufficiently out of reach.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I've been to so many different places. I've approached cities, entered barrens, icefields, and deserts all scattered with life...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: In every place I've been, the flames of war continue to burn. I have witnessed every forgotten end.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Over the course of my long journey, I've never put down my cello.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I've played for all kinds of people from all walks of life, but the end result has never been satisfactory.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A strong soul, rationality without reservation, a pure and sincere openness... I strive to approach to that future, yet it is still so far away.

steps.name: Arturia?
steps.text: But you will die here, in a distant corner, in a dilapidated monastery. Death will reduce everything to naught, leaving not a trace behind.

steps.name: Arturia?
steps.text: Do you grip your cello to play your own requiem? With nothing but fear, helplessness, anger, and sorrow?

steps.name: Arturia?
steps.text: Just as you used to be.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The clouds are gathering outside the window again.

steps.name: Arturia?
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: We cannot hope to hold onto a single cloud. But, is it not the entire sky we seek to depict?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Great men must die, just as ordinary men must die. Those who've walked with us through life will eventually part ways, and none may overwrite death.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Death will cut the threads of our lives and turn our bodies into hollow shells, incapable of harboring thoughts or feelings, incapable of forming new substance.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But, this does not mean that the complex and profound emotions we once held will completely disappear.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Precisely because death is insurmountable, I must play, and continue to play. This way, those dissipated feelings will continue to be felt, understood, and remembered by all.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Is that not its very purpose?

steps.name: Arturia?
steps.text: Arturia, have you considered that what you just saw might actually be your future?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I'm glad that I'm finally getting closer to it.

The sound of strings continues to reverberate through the woods. The Sankta slowly places her cello into its case as the Cautus girl watches her movements in silence, waiting for her to make eye contact.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Amiya?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Sorry for getting you wrapped up in my melody...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Arturia, we haven't had a chance for formal introductions since you came to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I believe today's occasion makes for a perfect icebreaker, better than any deliberate arrangement.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Your powers are strange. You don't even need an instrument...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It's like...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Two mirrors.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Simple, yes, but through them, you can see countless selves.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You, and Rhodes Island, are a lot more interesting than I thought.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I can say the same thing about your music... Even in such a short period of time, it feels like we've gotten to know each other quite well.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Do you feel those emotions often? Do you understand how I think?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But in the end, we're still rather different.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Such a shame.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But we'll have plenty of time to spend together.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Now then, please hurry back with me.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: There's no need to rush. I'm not trying to get away.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The fact is, you've been away from the landship for a long time.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: And, it just so happens that there's a distinguished Lateran guest who wants to see you.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We've been looking all over for you...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I see. My apologies, then.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Amiya, after we get back to the ship, do you think I could invite you to my concert?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You could be more than just an audience.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Sure. We welcome all who have good will towards Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Do you see me as one such person?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No, your thoughts go beyond good and evil. That, I'm well aware of.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But, let me be clear on that one point.
Nobody would mention any of the events that just transpired. After a piece, there is always some tacit understanding among the performers, and among the audience.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I quite like the view here. Too bad I won't be able to stay any longer.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Let's go.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A 'distinguished guest' indeed.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Looks like Amiya is more capable than I gave her credit for.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It is an honor... Holy Father.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: To the Infected children who just ran by, I was nothing more than 'The Grandpa with the Lateran Candy.'

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: No 'Holy Father' here. Just a grandpa.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: As you wish.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Arturia Giallo. I believe this is the first time we've met.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: But you don't seem surprised.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I get the sense that your trip to Leithanien has brought you a wealth of experience and broadened your horizons.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: If it had something to do with me, and had to be personally arranged by the leader of Rhodes Island... I figured it was probably a very important person.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Though, I expected a meeting like this would take place in the Basilica's Hall of Pontifical Audiences, where the Holy Father would hand down his sentence to a dangerous repeat blasphemer.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: It's true that the Notarial Hall has logged far too many anomalous incidents that involve you.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: When Federico brought you back to Laterano, the Curia immediately organized the First, Fifth, Sixth, and Seventh Tribunals to conduct a joint trial.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: All according to the law, of course.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: 'The law'.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: So before that happens, we should meet at least once. And Rhodes Island is the only place where that could happen.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Arturia, daughter of sin. For the time being, you can think of this dormitory as a makeshift confessional.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: What we say here will not be recorded, and will not be acknowledged hereafter.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I've had an awakening.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Without ritual, or witnesses. But that's fine. You were no hero to begin with.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: On behalf of Laterano, I pronounce you, Arturia Giallo...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Our next chosen Saint.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I get the feeling you don't do this willingly.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: What makes you say that?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Though, it doesn't really matter. There will always be some meaning behind the law's choices.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Federico was the one who brought you to Rhodes Island, right?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Funny. I wonder how you explained to our darling Saint that the fugitive he had just apprehended was also chosen to be a Saint?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Or, maybe...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: You're right, Federico doesn't know yet.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: But, he will understand. I will ask that of him.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: After all, I am neither condoning nor forgiving the things you've done, my child.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I never cared for the law's forgiveness, or this... title. It's all rather annoying, to be entirely honest.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What else will the Curia be using me for?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Child...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: There is much you do not understand. Your experiences, behaviors, ideals, and even the paranoia reflected in your Arts...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Have all appeared countless times before – one particular interpretation by Sankta, unto Sankta.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: How can you be so sure that your unique talents, your unique Arts... are not a deliberate manifestation of the law?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: After all, you carry a halo over your head. You are a Lateran Sankta, Arturia.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The white walls of Laterano have stood for thousands of years, and you are not the only, uh, 'Alienus,' as much I loathe the word.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Nevertheless, our glorious law has given me a decisive answer.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And what does this vague 'answer' mean, Your Holiness?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: It means...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: That every light we know will one day be extinguished.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: And it is no exception.
The old Pope playfully points to the halo hovering above his head.
Arturia is lost in thought.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Even if everything about the Sankta existence is interpreted as 'its' boon?
The Pope does not answer, simply moving abruptly to his next question.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: What will you be?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I... What?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Take away your prejudice, your pride, and your sins – and what will be left of you? What would you do? What would you bring?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Answer me this.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I'm still searching, Holy Father.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: There's no point in lying to you. But, you say that our halos will fade... and that the Sankta will lose the cozy cabin of their faith?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Wouldn't that just make Laterano the same as any other place?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: My ideal 'understanding', my ideal 'emotion', the kind of unreserved, pure, and honest... 'communication' that I seek...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Has nothing to do with what you just said. Not even a little bit.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And yet, why does the law insist on choosing me as a so-called 'Saint'?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Mm... All I can say is, you're right.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: You gave a much more reasonable answer than I expected. It would appear that what transpired in Leithanien was much more extreme than what was officially documented in our intel.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And... what if I refuse to become a Saint?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Or, is this the 'atonement' that you've arranged for me, and I don't have the right to refuse?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Child, the choice is still yours to make.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I am simply conveying the warning I've received to a fellow citizen of Laterano.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You, who stands atop all the Operae, would turn to a sinner?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: But, as you know, the Pope has ways of cleverly manipulating the words of a revelation, for example, by changing the name of the Saint.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to threaten you. Federico will see the case through regardless.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: If you really think that, then why––

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: ––But, when the sun sets, your thoughts and beliefs may prove to be a potent medicine.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The 'Saint' is a sign that the Sankta are in peril. All I can do is tinker around the edges.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Furthermore, the tragedy that you caused was also your own tragedy.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Sankta, Laterano, faith, empathy, communication, and our society. These things comprise your story. They comprise you.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Is there any Pope who would turn a blind eye to all this?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: So, after deep reflection, I decided to personally see you to the end, young Saint. Until your duty is done.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I will lead all of you to the future you deserve.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What is that end?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Don't know. Prophecy isn't part of the job.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Having that said... going off of recent developments, the future you deserve is far from bright.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It seems like this decision has been a heavy burden on your shoulders.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The situation might just be bad enough to necessitate the gamble.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: How does that sound to you, Arturia?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Would you consider... becoming an audience for a Saint?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I'm not particularly well-versed in music, but... Actually, wait a minute...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I've been standing for too long. Why don't we head to Rhodes Island's cozy reception area for a bit?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You can listen while we walk.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Fine, fine. Hup.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Please begin, then. I'd like to hear something distinctly 'Lateran.'
Through the window, the daylight's tail end stubbornly leaves its outline in the sky, the dusk shimmering brilliantly.
For no particular reason, she thinks of the sunsets in Zwillingstürme, and the clouds above many cities she has seen.
The sky is getting dark, and a slight shaking comes from underfoot, indicating that the landship is about to sail into the night.
The bridge lights come on.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Now then...
A melody begins to flow.
